records.our_prose: Cayenne is a moderate feeder rather than a heavy one, and the timing matters more than the amount. Work a complete fertilizer such as 1 to 2 pounds of 10-10-10 per 100 square feet, or a few inches of compost, into the bed before transplanting. Then side-dress lightly with nitrogen about 3 to 4 weeks after planting and again once the first pods have set. The cardinal rule is to go easy on nitrogen: too much gives a big, bushy, leafy plant with plenty of foliage but few blooms and little fruit, the single most common pepper-feeding mistake. Pair modest feeding with steady moisture, since even watering, not extra fertilizer, is what fills clean pods and heads off blossom-end rot.
